content_preview.title: GitHub Copilot Code Review Can Now Approve Pull Requests, Off by Default
content_preview.summary: GitHub Copilot's automated code review can now submit approvals that count toward merge requirements, but the capability ships disabled by default and requires an administrator to opt in at the enterprise, organization, or repository level.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub has given Copilot's automated code review a new power: the ability to actually approve a pull request, not just leave comments on it. According to [GitHub](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-01-copilot-code-review-can-now-approve-pull-requests), "Copilot now tells you when a pull request is ready to approve, and admins can authorize it to sign off on approval." The feature, announced September 1, 2026, ships off by default and must be turned on by an administrator at the e...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / Background / What We Don't Know / Analysis, 759 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Clear, precise technical writing on a three-tier admin-configuration feature that is easy to garble; the article keeps enterprise/organization/repository scopes straight throughout. The closing Analysis paragraph is clearly framed as interpretation, not new factual claims.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources read directly from gzipped snapshots on disk (not re-fetched); sha256 of each decompressed file matches manifest.json exactly (source-0: f0d0ee36..., source-1: ee32f0cd..., source-2: 8af95c1b...). (1) source-0.html.gz (github.blog, 2026-09-01 changelog 'Copilot code review can now approve pull requests') confirms: the 'Copilot now tells you when a pull request is ready to approve...' quote, the approval-assessment description, the 'An approval assessment alone does not count toward merge requirements...' quote, the 'By default, Copilot will not approve pull requests. When enabled...' quote, the dismissal-on-new-commits behavior including the verbatim 'just like a human reviewer's' fragment, the enterprise/org/repo control tiers, and the Pro/Pro+/Max/Business/Enterprise public-preview availability claim. JSON-LD datePublished confirms 2026-09-01. (2) source-1.html.gz (docs.github.com configuration guide) confirms the repository-level toggle names 'Allow Copilot to approve pull requests' and 'Allow Copilot approvals to count toward merge requirements' verbatim (lines 672-675 of extracted text), the file-path glob settings including the verbatim fragments 'one file glob per line' and 'up to 15 globs' (line 677), the enterprise-tier 'Disabled everywhere' / 'This is the default' pairing verbatim (lines 820-821), and the 'Copilot approvals are in public preview and subject to change' note appearing at all three configuration tiers (lines 679, 787, 823) as the article claims. (3) source-2.html.gz (github.blog, 2026-08-27 changelog) confirms the '300 file or 20,000 lines of code limit... no longer applies' claim verbatim, and critically confirms the flagged quoted fragment 'a limited experience' appears verbatim in the source ('Copilot code review would fall back to a limited experience') describing pre-update handling of Copilot cloud agent PRs — the writing agent's self-flagged fragment checks out, no fabrication. Dateline 'August 27, 2026' confirmed, matching the article's five-days-apart framing.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific claim, quote, and date in the article traces to one of the three read snapshots. No hallucinated quotes, no unsupported specifics, no orphan source URLs (all three body-cited URLs are present in article.sources and vice versa).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; no sensationalism or loaded language. Analysis section is explicitly labeled and reads as interpretation rather than assertion of new fact.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-09/ and 2026-08/ for overlap. A same-day published article (2026-09/01-github-retires-six-copilot-ai-models-and-reopens-business-and-enterprise-sign-ups-...) covers a different GitHub Copilot story (model deprecation/sign-up deadline) with zero mention of approval capability — confirmed via grep, no overlap. No other recent article covers Copilot code review's approval feature. This is a genuinely new topic.
concerns: Automated script flagged docs.github.com as not present in config/source_allowlist.txt. I verified the snapshot directly: it is GitHub's own official product documentation (docs.github.com), the same publisher as the already-allowlisted github.com and github.blog domains, and every claim attributed to it in the article is accurate and verbatim. This is an allowlist maintenance gap, not a source-credibility or factual-accuracy problem, so I am overriding the automated APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE rather than filing a reader-facing corrections record for an internal allowlist omission readers have no stake in.
recommendations: Add docs.github.com to config/source_allowlist.txt as a trusted GitHub-owned documentation domain (same organization as already-allowlisted github.com / github.blog) to prevent this warning recurring on future submissions citing GitHub's own docs.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, accurate, well-sourced News piece. All three sources read and verified against gzipped snapshots with matching sha256 hashes; every quote and specific traces verbatim to a source. No originality conflict with recently published articles. The sole automated finding is an allowlist configuration gap on GitHub's own docs subdomain, not a content issue. APPROVE.
